title: From Crystallization to the Ontology Boundary
subtitle: Three experiment sets trace where active symbolic world models work, where neural proposals help, and where the assumptions finally break.
excerpt: A preservation-first account of 38 standalone experiment programs spanning automata learning, crystallized planning, symbolic abstraction, ontology acquisition, and exact certification—including every negative, null, interrupted, and failed result.
lede: The archive began with a strong recurring idea: query a learned or hidden world, compress its behavior into an executable symbolic theory, and use contradictions to revise that theory. Across three notebooks, the idea succeeds repeatedly when the state space, grammar, reset operation, or verification contract is supplied. The most informative result arrives when those supports are removed: the ontology-free bootstrap fails across state discovery, graph recovery, transfer, and novelty handling. The record therefore narrows the claim rather than erasing the progress.

entries.label: Entry 01
entries.title: The first result was that these were experiment archives, not ordinary notebooks.
entries.dek: Thirty-eight standalone experiment programs, several revisions, concatenated scripts, interrupted runs, and output/source mismatches had to be separated before the science could be summarized honestly.

blocks.markdown:
The three source files contained 40 code cells, of which 37 were nonempty. Two cells each concatenated two complete programs, yielding **38 standalone experiment programs plus one artifact-display utility**. There were no explanatory Markdown cells. Execution counts were non-monotone, global names were repeatedly redefined, and many programs wrote to the same transient `/content` directories. Embedded PNGs and verbose logs accounted for most of the 4.8 MB archive.

The cleanup kept every nonempty program and its original cell index, stripped stored outputs only after a cell-by-cell scientific audit, added section and provenance cells, separated concatenated programs, and moved artifacts into collision-free relative directories. The three original SHA-256 hashes are recorded in notebook metadata. Full textual outputs, including all 81 V5 gate configurations, remain in the published scientific records.

blocks.label: Evidence rule
blocks.markdown: A repaired cell is reproducible code, not retroactive evidence. The deterministic FP32 arithmetic cell still has **no completed scientific result** because its archived source failed to parse. The V13 dtype repair follows the completed V13.1 correction, but the failed V13 run remains failed. Likewise, the V6 export fix present in the stored source was not validated by the older output that stopped during CSV writing.

blocks.title: Reproducibility scope
blocks.body: All programs parse in the cleaned notebooks and all registered settings, seeds, controls, and metrics are retained. Exact bitwise replay is not promised where the historical runs used AMP, BF16, TF32, cuDNN benchmarking, GPU-specific branches, unpinned dependencies, or a single seed.
blocks.meta: Historical experiment record; not peer reviewed. Fast/dev modes are smoke tests, not substitutes for the recorded full runs.

entries.label: Entry 02
entries.title: Exact finite theories were recoverable; useful abstractions were conditional and sometimes harmful.
entries.dek: The first set moves from contradiction-driven automata revision through shared representations and reusable Boolean languages to extracting symbolic behavior from neural endpoints.

blocks.markdown:
**Residual NFA revision.** An inherited 22-state/64-arc theory with bounded accuracy 0.9663 was replaced in two rounds by an exact 9-state theory after 299 membership queries. The capacity-bounded variant also succeeded, with a one-arc version difference that remains unexplained rather than averaged away.

**Mealy revision and its null control.** A 24-complexity inherited transducer collapsed to the exact six-state/twelve-arc world in two rounds. The uncapped control followed the identical trajectory, so the hard capacity limit had **no observed causal effect** in this run.

**Unification and frame invention.** Bit-coded W-method experiments recovered a shared six-state latent machine across four renamed views, reducing 392 separate-description bits to 215 and recovering every hidden action translation. Unrelated worlds remained separate. A supplied register-program DSL then compressed four related 436-bit flat tables to a 138-bit `(2,3)` coordinate program while rejecting unrelated unification.

**Reusable Boolean languages.** Paid NAND-derived macros recovered the planted mechanism in 8/9 families. Related code cost fell to 0.521 of baseline, but the evaluation-count confidence interval included no advantage and unrelated evaluation cost worsened to 1.792×. Sequential worlds produced two correct reusable gates, cutting related transfer cost 21→6, evaluations 73,876→3,480, and queries 12→8.33. A broader sample-complexity experiment found a strong semantics×price interaction, but two registered predictions failed: a disjoint vocabulary modestly helped rather than hurt, and the expensive correct vocabulary did not approximate baseline closely enough.

**Fallible adoption.** A first broad endpoint misleadingly reported an MDL-positive library everywhere. The corrected planted-XOR/XNOR endpoint showed that target-library optimality collapsed with contamination and noise—for example, at fully related data it fell from 1.00 with no noise to 0.03 at 20% noise. Whenever the target was globally optimal, the greedy learner found it; the failure was evidential support, not local search.

**Neural endpoints.** Symbolic regression recovered `force/mass` from analytic and three trained black boxes and rejected a random-network control, yet macros did not reduce the stable query count. A five-state DFA extracted from each of three imperfect transformers had perfect sampled truth generalization while matching each endpoint's imperfect long-sequence behavior; bounded certification must not be confused with proof at every length.

blocks.alt: Bar chart comparing three transformers and their extracted symbolic DFAs on bounded and long hidden-language accuracy, beside the five-state extracted DFA graph.
blocks.caption: The extracted five-state DFAs scored perfectly against the hidden language on the sampled long test while the neural endpoints remained imperfect. This is bounded/sample evidence of symbolic denoising, not proof of equivalence at every length.
blocks.provenance: Original embedded PNG from NFAWorldModel.ipynb, source cell 14 (tiny transformer to symbolic DFA).

blocks.markdown: **Evolving neural arithmetic.** A single-seed study extracted the exact five-state ADD/SUB machine from a recurrent neural endpoint. The ten-seed replication found first exact machines at epochs 10–19, often before sustained ≥.99 neural mastery, but the preregistered canonical four-state carry/borrow waypoint occurred in **0/10 seeds**. A paired learning-rate study again found zero canonical waypoints across 20 arms: slow learning produced frequent undersplitting; fast learning more often produced direct or oversplit paths. Among nine eligible fast-arm seeds, faithful exact extraction preceded mastery in 6/9. Many intermediate extractions hit the state cap or remained exactly wrong despite high sampled neural accuracy. The attempted deterministic FP32 rewrite did not run because its source had a syntax error.

blocks.alt: Three-panel paired learning-rate result showing extracted state complexity, predeclared outcome fractions for slow and fast arms, and faithful exact recovery step versus neural mastery step.
blocks.caption: The claim-closing run replaces the unsupported canonical-waypoint story with a directional result: slow arms undersplit more often, while fast arms more often reached direct exact or oversplit paths. Points below the diagonal in the right panel are cases where neural mastery came first.
blocks.provenance: Original embedded PNG from NFAWorldModel.ipynb, source cell 17 (paired learning-rate claim-closing experiment).

groups.title: Supported in these controlled worlds
items: Contradiction-driven finite-state learners can replace larger inherited theories with compact exact observable models.
MDL can recognize shared structure across renamed interfaces and pay for abstractions that transfer to related synthetic tasks.
Symbolic extraction can denoise a neural endpoint when the behavioral class and verification interface are controlled.

groups.title: Not supported
items: The model-capacity intervention caused the observed Mealy recovery.
Learned vocabularies universally reduce search cost or help unrelated tasks.
Neural arithmetic learning passes through a canonical four-state theory-revision waypoint.
Recovered automata reveal internal neural representations rather than observable behavioral shadows.

entries.label: Entry 03
entries.title: Crystallized planning held up; open-world rule invention did not know when to abstain.
entries.dek: The second set turns exact symbolic tables into planners and homeostatic memories, then calibrates when a persistent change should rewrite the model.

blocks.markdown:
The original crystallization task gave both a finite machine and neural beam search 100% planning success, but median plans were only three steps and success allowed reaching the target position at any depth. The corrected protocol required an exact terminal state at an exact sampled horizon. The extracted 65-state machine remained perfect; neural beam success fell to **26.25%** while machine graph search stayed at **100%**, despite neural random-rollout state accuracy remaining 99.90% at horizon 128. The corrected experiment supersedes the easy planning claim.

A prospective monitor predicted entry into a visible but symbolically omitted wind zone. Joint observation+action AUROC declined from .998 at one step to .922 at twelve, risky plans outranked paired safe plans 92.47% of the time, and joint tie-breaking cut actual exits from 47.5% to 22.25%. Yet only 74.5% of exits were prospectively detected, and held-out safe FPR was 5.78% against a 5% validation target. The unobservable-switch control stayed at chance. This is a statistical monitor, not a safety guarantee.

Homeostatic re-grounding reduced single-shock integrated error from 19.596 to 1.000 and recovered 100%; the neural observer with the same observation benefited identically, so there is no symbolic exclusivity result. A balanced escalation policy reached 93.75% taxonomy accuracy with zero false L1/L2 revision and 98.83% permanent-change revision. Equal-budget active repair covered more transitions and slightly improved global accuracy (38.75% vs 36.11%) but was worse on-policy (39.21% vs 51.19%); neither learned a globally good table.

Runtime MDL gating fixed that failure only because the candidate change family was supplied. Under transient shocks, naive patches grew to 118.36 states and 86.69% planning while the gated model stayed at 65 states and 100%. After a permanent force change, naive growth reached 296.35 states and 15.60% planning; the gate adopted one global rule after 33.91 steps and restored 100%. A full 81-setting calibration found exactly 27 feasible settings—all support-24 configurations. Extra confirmation probes added delay and queries without benefit once persistent support was sufficient.

blocks.caption: The corrected exact-horizon experiment retained a 100% accurate finite transition table and exposed a planning gap hidden by near-perfect random rollouts: machine planning was 100%, neural beam planning 26.25%.

items.label: wrong adoption on both out-of-grammar controls

blocks.label: The decisive V6 boundary
blocks.markdown: Grammar synthesis recovered representable changes exactly in 97.5% of active and passive trials; active did **not** beat passive, so registered P2 failed. Worse, parity and random-local-table controls were both outside the grammar yet a wrong in-grammar approximation was adopted in 100% of trials, with only 54.7%/56.2% transition accuracy and 18.9%/16.6% planning. The system could synthesize inside a supplied class but could not recognize that the class was wrong.

groups.title: Supported
items: A supplied-state finite machine can preserve exact long-horizon planning when a finite-width neural planner fails.
Prospective validity benefits from joint state/action context and can improve plan selection before a manifest contradiction.
Persistent-support gates can prevent transient overreaction and adopt a supplied compressed global change.

groups.title: Unsupported or failed
items: The prospective monitor provides formal safety.
Active V6 synthesis beats passive synthesis.
V6 detects or refuses dynamics outside its grammar.
The V6 run fully saved its declared artifacts; the archived execution stopped during CSV export.

entries.label: Entry 04
entries.title: Quotient transfer scaled; autonomous ontology discovery collapsed.
entries.dek: The third set extends the mechanism to language, large quotient spaces, raw observations, exact conformance, and non-enumerable program entropy.

blocks.markdown:
**V10.1 was interrupted.** On Tiny Shakespeare, GRU selection NLL was 1.8934 versus nanoGPT 2.4527 at step 100/2,000, but the run stopped during the next batch. No symbolic machine, hybrid gate, final validation, generation, or registered verdict exists. The early neural comparison is not a completed crystallization result.

**V11 quotient transfer.** Four canonical templates compressed 1,728 raw bits to 703.2 bits (2.46×). Active and random both had median seven queries, but exact@8 was 100% versus 78.1%; the benefit was tail/fixed-budget success, not median cost. Novel detection was actually 95.8% for active versus 100% for dual and random by twelve queries. A repeated novel family was promoted after three worlds with zero promotions from twelve transient worlds.

**V12 text8.** A one-pass variable-order MDL state machine scaled from 24,902 retained states at 1M characters to 832,572 at 90M. Test bpc improved from 2.1736 to 1.6359; top-1 accuracy reached 64.31%; deep order≤12 beat order≤4 (1.6359 vs 1.9762 bpc); and transition audits were exact. This was not a neural comparison, and two complete revisions had been concatenated and overwrote one artifact directory.

**V13/V13.1.** The first BF16 implementation failed before training because BF16 messages were accumulated into float tensors. The corrected V13.1 turned 47.57% local neural table accuracy into 91.7% exact active crystallization at median eight observations, recovered all four recurring templates, and reached 100% unseen exact@8. Increasing proposal top-k was a material change: exact crystallization rose from 79.2% to 91.7%. An appended older V13 rerun and a nominally same-seed continuation were interrupted; their slight differences show that bitwise GPU reproducibility was not established.

**V14 was the strongest negative result.** Without supplied state labels/count, action-effect labels/count, family labels, or a candidate grammar, mixture clustering looked promising (ARI .843) but behavioral ARI fell to .782, exact state count was only 22.2%, graph accuracy 15.3%, and all twelve prior graphs appeared unique. No recurring grammar was learned. Active and random both achieved 33.3% exact at median 25/36; novelty was never safely rejected or promoted. Predictions P1–P8 all failed. The printed `future exact=43/42` was a sentinel meaning “not reached,” not supernumerary success.

blocks.markdown:
**V16 narrowed the problem.** With an exact synthetic equivalence oracle, monotone suffix refinement recovered all 32 tested Moore machines up to 24 states; median membership queries rose from 89.5 at six states to 560 at 24. V16.1 replaced that oracle with charged W-method testing under a supplied eight-state bound. Every method certified exactly, but neural ranking used 829 median interactions—31.1% worse than the simple length heuristic, though 21.2% better than random. Charging 567,117 prior interactions made the amortized neural end-to-end cost 18,551 interactions per test.

**V16.2 scaled entropy without enumeration.** At 20–80 program bits, Transformer token accuracy stayed near 98% while exact proposal rate fell from 90.6% to 76.9%; the local MLP fell from 83.8% to 54.6%. Twenty random hashes plus exact fallback produced 100% empirical correctness and no wrong accepts, with a fixed-wrong-proposal bound of $2^{-20}$, but fallback and mean query cost rose with entropy. Absolute exactness still required all $H$ identity bits. Training consumed 20,661,504 module observations—4,132 amortized per test program. The module ontology, four-bit identities, reset, and parity-hash interface were all supplied.

groups.title: Supported
items: Quotient representations can compress and transfer deterministic finite laws across unseen coordinate relabelings.
Deep MDL-selected suffix states scale to text8 and improve held-out compression over shallow contexts.
Neural proposals can be error-corrected into exact finite tables when the ontology, grammar, query cells, and candidate budget are supplied.
Exact/PAC symbolic verification can be kept logically separate from a neural proposal score.

groups.title: Not supported
items: The Tiny Shakespeare hybrid completed or beat its components.
Active novelty search always beats random search.
The earlier transfer gains survive autonomous ontology and grammar acquisition.
Neural W-method ranking beats the shortest-test baseline or repays its prior-acquisition cost.
V16.2 demonstrates ontology-free, real-environment program discovery.

entries.label: Entry 05
entries.title: The coherent conclusion is conditional usefulness, not autonomous symbolic intelligence.
entries.dek: The final pass treats every control, failure, incomplete run, and supplied interface as part of the result.

blocks.markdown:
Across the archive, finite-state learning, MDL compression, invariant quotienting, and neural-to-symbolic extraction repeatedly work when the learner receives a controlled contract: a resettable deterministic world, a state/action ontology, a finite grammar or DSL, an upper state bound, exact membership access, a parity-hash oracle, or private ground truth for audit. Those are valuable engineering and scientific results.

The strongest attempted assumption removal—V14—fails. The strongest open-world control—V6 out-of-grammar dynamics—fails by confidently adopting the wrong rule. The most direct learned-query comparison—V16.1—loses to length ordering once tested fairly and becomes extremely expensive when prior acquisition is charged. These outcomes do not cancel the earlier successes; they locate their boundary.

The scientific record also separates three forms of “exact”: formal finite equivalence, exactness conditional on a declared state bound/test suite, and perfect accuracy on a bounded or sampled audit. It separates learner-visible evidence from private ground-truth diagnostics. And it keeps incomplete source revisions out of the positive evidence count.

items.name: Calibrated abstention outside the grammar
items.design: Repeat V6 with held-out representable rules and multiple unrepresentable families. Require a calibrated residual/evidence threshold that can return unknown; compare adoption, abstention, transition accuracy, and planning under fixed budgets.
items.decisionValue: Determines whether symbolic invention can avoid the 100% wrong-adoption failure before any broader open-world claim.

items.name: Factorized ontology recovery
items.design: Replace V14's clustering-first pipeline with joint representation, intervention, and predictive-state refinement. Freeze train/test renderers and report ontology cost together with conditional transfer cost across seeds.
items.decisionValue: Tests whether V14 failed because of the specific bootstrap or because the information contract is inadequate.

items.name: Matched query-policy baselines
items.design: Compare neural, length, random, entropy, and handcrafted structural rankings on the same W-method suite, with training acquisition, calibration, resets, actions, and wall time fully charged.
items.decisionValue: Establishes when a learned proposal channel has positive end-to-end value rather than merely beating random.

items.name: Multi-seed deterministic replication pack
items.design: Rerun selected CPU-exact and GPU-sensitive experiments in containers with dataset hashes, dependency locks, serialized worlds/splits, query transcripts, and deterministic/AMP paired modes.
items.decisionValue: Separates stable qualitative phenomena from single-seed or hardware-dependent trajectories.

blocks.title: Final evidential status
blocks.body: The archive supports controlled finite-world learning, compression, transfer, and verification. It does not yet support robust autonomous ontology discovery, unrestricted concept invention, internal neural-state interpretation, or real-world scientific-law discovery.
blocks.meta: All claims were checked against source cells, stored outputs, controls, errors, and version differences. Detailed records are published with the notebooks.

blocks.markdown: A failed assumption-removal experiment is not a detour from the research program. It is the point where the program finally says what it still needs.

The cleaned notebooks preserve source-level provenance and remove stored outputs only after their scientific content was captured. No failed or interrupted run is presented as completed evidence.
The exhaustive cell-indexed audits and machine-readable cell manifests are available in `notebooks/records/`; they are the authority when this narrative summary omits a secondary metric.
